newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CANBERRA WATCH - Tax push costs votes, Labor winning on industry.
newsitem.headline: CANBERRA WATCH - Tax push costs votes, Labor winning on industry.

text.p: The Australian government is losing ground on some crucial issues, most importantly taxation and unemployment, an opinion poll published on Tuesday shows.
The poll shows an overall picture of the Liberal-Nation government generally rated ahead of the Labor opposition on most policy issues but slipping.
Among the four big voter-influencing issues, the government now has a decisive lead only on the subject of interest rates, the Newspoll in The Australian newspaper shows.
The general slippage is perhaps only consistent with falling voting-intention support for the government in recent opinion polls, but the results raise two very important observations:
--The government's recent push for tax reform is probably repelling more voters than it is attracting, despite all the positive hype.
--The Labor Party's shift to interventionism on industry policy is lifting its standing on the crucial issue of unemployment.
Each side has decisive leads on minor issues, but any analysis must identify the issues that really influence votes.

This table shows how far the government leads the opposition on various issues and how that lead has changed since January. The "voter influence" star rating is the result of a casual survey of Canberra journalists and political operators.
